overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair's affidavit showed he alone decided not to place the survey on an agenda, so no quorum deliberated and no minutes were required. Later-raised allegations were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee deliberated outside a noticed meeting when it decided not to act on a community survey about the superintendent.
allegations.key_passage: Here, Mr. Kelley provided an affidavit stating that he alone made the decision not to add the survey to a Committee agenda.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to create minutes of the survey-related deliberations it was said to have held outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because no deliberation between or among a quorum of the Committee members took place, the Committee was not required to create minutes.

allegations.summary: Request for further review added claims that minutes were not made available within the required time and that the committee did not meet to review the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Because these allegations were not contained in the original complaint filed with the Committee, we do not review them now.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
